in_english.name: Qutuz
in_english.meaning: Strong and powerful in battle, warrior
in_english.long_meaning: The name Qutuz originates from Arabic roots, specifically from the verb 'qatala', meaning to fight or struggle. It signifies someone who is strong, powerful, and resilient in battle. Historically, Qutuz was the name of a Mamluk Sultan of Egypt who played a significant role in the Islamic world during the 13th century. The name is associated with bravery, leadership, and determination.

data.cultural_impact: The name Qutuz holds great significance in Islamic history as it is the name of Sultan Qutuz who played a pivotal role in the 13th century by leading the Mamluks (slaves turned soldiers) to a victorious battle against the Mongols, reuniting the Islamic world after the disastrous invasion of the Seljuk Sultanate by the Mongols.
data.spiritual_significance: A name that signifies the powerful triumph over darkness (represented in the form of adversaries or challenges), and a reminder of the investiture of divine trust in individuals, preparing them to be victors in their spiritual quests and battles of life. This name promotes courage, strength, and determination in the face of adversity.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Qutuz was a Mamluk Sultan of Egypt and Syria from 1290 to 1294 AD. He rose to power after defeating his previous master, Qalawun, in battle and gaining control of his army.
historical_references.context: Mamluk Sultan of Egypt and Syria

historical_references.reference: Qutuz is most famous for leading the Mamluks to a decisive victory over the Mongol invasion led by Hulagu Khan in the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260 AD. This battle marked the first time the Mongols were defeated in battle and prevented the further advance of their territories into the Middle East.
historical_references.context: Battle of Ain Jalut against Mongols
